rationales: Anatomy studies the internal structure of organisms.
Histology studies tissues, especially their microscopic structure.
Morphology studies the form and external structure of organisms.
Physiology studies how organisms and their parts function.
Sulphur is not the main element regulating stomatal opening and closing.
Potassium ions regulate the opening and closing of stomata.
Calcium is not the principal regulator identified in this question.
Phosphorus is not the main element regulating stomatal opening and closing.
Forestry concerns the management of forests, not farms.
Farming is the option that matches developing and maintaining different types of farms.
Horticulture concerns the cultivation of garden plants and crops.
Animal husbandry focuses on breeding and caring for livestock.
Hydrogen makes up about 10% of the mass of living organisms, not 18%.
Carbon makes up about 18% of the mass of living organisms.
Oxygen is the most abundant element in living organisms, at about 65%, not 18%.
Nitrogen makes up about 3% of the mass of living organisms, not 18%.
Observation is the basic starting step of the biological method.
Deduction is reasoning from a hypothesis or general principle to a specific result.
A hypothesis is a proposed explanation made after observations.
Experimentation tests a hypothesis and comes after earlier steps.
Prions are not composed of carbohydrates.
Prions are infectious agents composed of proteins.
Prions are not composed of fats.
Prions are not composed of minerals.
ATP is the major energy currency of cells.
FAD is an electron-carrying coenzyme, not the main energy currency.
Sunlight is an energy source for photosynthesis, not the energy currency used by cells.
NAD is an electron-carrying coenzyme, not the main energy currency.
Louis Pasteur did not first describe cells.
Rudolf Virchow contributed to cell theory but did not first describe cells.
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus, not cells themselves.
Robert Hooke first described cells after observing cork.
Ribosomes occur in both plant and animal cells and are not membrane-bounded.
Mitochondria occur in both plant and animal cells.
Plastids are membrane-bounded organelles found in plants and algae.
Endoplasmic reticulum occurs in both plant and animal cells.
Mitosis can contribute to regeneration.
Mitosis replaces worn-out or damaged cells.
Mitosis supports growth and development.
Halving the chromosome number is a result of meiosis, not mitosis.
A cofactor helps enzyme activity rather than increasing activation energy.
Breaking hydrogen bonds in proteins is not the defining role of a cofactor.
A cofactor helps and facilitates enzyme activity.
Cofactors are non-protein components, not proteins.
Stomata cover about 1–2% of the leaf surface.
The stated coverage is not 1–3%.
The stated coverage is not 1–4%.
The stated coverage is not 1–5%.
Vitamin A does not perform the stated role in mineral absorption and bone deposition.
Vitamin B is not the vitamin identified for this role.
Vitamin C supports iron absorption but is not the vitamin described for mineral deposition in bones.
Vitamin D promotes mineral absorption from the intestine and deposition in bones.
The stated proportion is not 85%.
The textbook figure for haemoglobin filling the red blood cell cytoplasm is about 90%.
The stated proportion is not 95%.
The cytoplasm is not 100% haemoglobin.
The biosphere is the global zone where life exists, not the diversity of plants.
A community consists of populations of different species living together.
Flora refers to the plant life of a particular region or period.
Fauna refers to the animal life of a particular region or period.
